We situate our approach within five related lines of research: fixed-rate model-based RL, variable-rate and temporal abstraction, learned skipping for planning, imagination quality improvement, and event-aware world models.

## 2.1 Model-Based RL with Fixed-Rate Imagination

Modern model-based RL agents learn latent world models and optimize policies through imagined rollouts at a fixed temporal resolution.

DreamerV3 \citep{hafner2023dreamerv3} learns a Recurrent State-Space Model (RSSM) that maintains deterministic and stochastic latent states, training an actor-critic purely through $H$-step imagined trajectories. It achieves strong performance across diverse domains but operates at a fixed one-environment-step-per-latent-step resolution, limiting the effective planning horizon to $H$ environment steps regardless of episode length. NE-Dreamer \citep{nedreamer2026} replaces pixel-level reconstruction with next-embedding prediction, yielding a decoder-free latent world model that improves sample efficiency while retaining the fixed-rate imagination structure. R2-Dreamer \citep{r2dreamer2026} similarly eliminates the observation decoder by training with redundancy-reduced latent targets, accelerating training and improving robustness.
These methods share a fundamental limitation: each imagination step covers exactly one environment timestep, so for long-horizon tasks (e.g., 250-step manipulation episodes), a rollout of $H{=}15$ steps covers only 6\% of the episode, creating a credit assignment bottleneck. Our method addresses this by learning to skip uneventful timesteps, extending the effective horizon to $\sum \Delta t_i$ environment steps (up to $H \times K$) without additional latent computation.

## 2.2 Variable-Rate and Temporal Abstraction

Several works introduce temporal flexibility into world model dynamics, either through externally specified time gaps or learned hierarchical abstractions.

TAWM \citep{freed2024tawm} introduces time-aware world models that condition latent dynamics on a temporal gap $\Delta t$ via RK4/Euler integration, enabling the model to predict across variable time scales. However, $\Delta t$ must be externally specified rather than learned, and TAWM is built on TD-MPC2's short-horizon MPC framework ($H{=}3$--$5$ with MPPI planning), where temporal skipping during planning is counterproductive. Our method adapts the variable-$\Delta t$ conditioning principle to DreamerV3's RSSM but makes $\Delta t$ \emph{state-dependent} via a learned event gate. THICK \citep{romac2024thick} learns a two-level temporal hierarchy via discrete latent dynamics, where the lower level forms invariant contexts and the upper level predicts context changes. While this achieves temporal abstraction, the fixed two-level structure cannot express continuous degrees of event significance or variable skip lengths within a single hierarchy level. HWM \citep{zhang2026hwm} extends this line by learning multi-scale latent world models for hierarchical planning with a learned action encoder for temporal compression, but similarly relies on a fixed two-level planner architecture. ASI \citep{neitz2018adaptive} learns to skip timesteps in recurrent dynamics models by min-pooling over reconstruction losses, selecting intervals that are easiest to predict. It operates on raw observation prediction without integration into a model-based RL loop and optimizes for prediction ease rather than dynamical significance.

Our approach avoids the multi-model exploitation problem identified by \citet{schiewer2024hierarchical} in hierarchical world models by operating within a single RSSM, while offering finer temporal adaptation than two-level hierarchies through a continuous per-step stride selection.

## 2.3 Learned Skipping for Planning

A separate line of work learns explicit skip or jump decisions to extend planning horizons.

LS-Imagine \citep{li2025lsimagine} learns jumping flags based on affordance-map kurtosis for open-world exploration in MineDojo, enabling the agent to skip over low-information states during imagination. The jumps are action-independent and designed for exploration in open-world settings. Our gate differs in two key ways: it operates within the actor-critic MBRL imagination loop with policy-dependent variable-rate stepping, and it selects strides based on latent-state dynamics rather than observation-space affordance maps. I-TAP \citep{itap2026} learns temporal abstractions via discrete residual tokens with an RQ-VAE, performing MCTS planning in token space for offline RL. It operates in a fundamentally different paradigm---offline and autoregressive---from our online RSSM-based approach.

While both LS-Imagine and I-TAP demonstrate the value of temporal flexibility in planning, neither addresses the specific setting of online actor-critic training with variable-rate latent imagination. Our event gate fills this gap by integrating state-dependent stride selection directly into DreamerV3's imagination pipeline.

## 2.4 Imagination Quality Improvement

Rather than changing temporal resolution, several recent works improve the quality of fixed-rate imagination rollouts.

DMWM \citep{wang2025dmwm} introduces a dual-mind architecture combining an RSSM-based System~1 for intuitive transitions with a logic-informed neural network (LINN) System~2 that provides logical reasoning feedback, improving long-horizon imagination coherence through logical constraints. It shares our motivation of extending effective RSSM imagination but addresses error accumulation at fixed temporal resolution rather than extending the temporal horizon. DyMoDreamer \citep{dymodreamer2025} uses inter-frame differencing masks with stochastic categorical dynamic modulation to focus RSSM attention on motion-relevant features, achieving strong results on visual benchmarks (Atari 100k, DMC). It operates at the observation/pixel level to improve per-step representation quality, whereas our method operates in latent space and changes the \emph{temporal resolution} of imagination rather than the attention quality of individual steps---the two approaches target complementary axes of improvement and could in principle be combined. ELVIS \citep{du2026elvis} introduces ensemble-calibrated uncertainty-aware $\lambda$-return gating for long-horizon RSSM-based MPC, adaptively weighting bootstrapping versus continued rollout based on epistemic uncertainty. While ELVIS adapts \emph{how much} to trust each imagination step, it does not change \emph{how many} environment steps each imagination step covers---our gate modifies the temporal resolution itself.

## 2.5 Event-Aware World Models

Event-driven representations have recently been applied to world models, though primarily at the observation level.

## FiGAR: Fine Grained Action Repetition

FiGAR is a novel framework which enables the agent to decide the action as well as the time scale of repeating it. The full paper title is "Learning to Repeat: Fine Grained Action Repetition for Deep Reinforcement Learning."

### Key Contributions

FiGAR can be used for improving any Deep Reinforcement Learning algorithm which maintains an explicit policy estimate by enabling temporal abstractions in the action space.

### Empirical Validation

The paper demonstrates performance improvements on top of three policy search algorithms in different domains: Asynchronous Advantage Actor Critic in the Atari 2600 domain, Trust Region Policy Optimization in Mujoco domain and Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient.

### Technical Details

FiGAR jointly learns an action policy and a second repetition policy that decides how often to repeat an action. Its repetition policy is not conditioned on the chosen action resulting in independent repetition and behaviour actions. The policies are learned together through a joint loss.

### Publication

The paper was published at ICLR 2017 (arXiv paper 1702.06054) by Sharma, Lakshminarayanan, and Ravindran. The paper is available on arXiv and OpenReview.

## I-TAP Paper

I-TAP (In-Context Latent Temporal-Abstraction Planner) is an offline RL framework that unifies in-context adaptation with online planning in a learned discrete temporal-abstraction space.

The paper proposes I-TAP as an offline RL method that learns a residual-quantized temporal abstraction and a context-conditioned latent dynamics model from offline trajectories via an observation-conditioned RQ-VAE and an autoregressive temporal Transformer, and instantiates an in-context planner that performs Monte Carlo Tree Search directly over latent tokens.

## Key Components

I-TAP learns an observation-conditioned residual-quantization VAE (RQ-VAE) that discretizes observation–macro-action sequences into a coarse-to-fine stack of residual tokens, together with a residual-quantized temporal Transformer that autoregressively predicts these tokens from recent observation and macro-action histories.

## Planning Approach

By taking expectations over futures under the learned latent dynamics, MCTS decouples action selection from noisy return estimates, explicitly handles uncertainty induced by partial observability, and provides a principled way to override suboptimal priors when predicted returns justify it.

The paper was recently published in February 2026 and is available on arXiv (2602.18694) and OpenReview. The research addresses challenges in planning-based reinforcement learning by working with latent temporal abstractions rather than primitive time scales.

## Overview

HWM (Hierarchical Planning with Latent World Models) is a framework for zero-shot hierarchical model predictive control using learned latent world models.

## Key Innovation

Rather than learning hierarchical policies, HWM introduces temporal hierarchy directly at inference time by planning over multiple timescales on task-agnostic world models trained via next-latent prediction. HWM learns world models operating at different temporal resolutions within a shared latent space, enabling a direct coupling between levels: high-level predictions act as subgoals for low-level MPC via latent-state matching.

## How It Works

A high-level planner optimizes macro-actions using a long-horizon world model to reach the goal; the first predicted latent state serves as a subgoal for a low-level planner, which optimizes primitive actions with a short-horizon world model.

## Problem It Addresses

Learned world models often struggle with long-horizon control due to the accumulation of prediction errors and the exponentially growing search space. HWM addresses these challenges by learning latent world models at multiple temporal scales and performing hierarchical planning across these scales, enabling long-horizon reasoning while substantially reducing inference-time planning complexity.

## Results

This hierarchical approach enables zero-shot control on real-world non-greedy robotic tasks, achieving a 70% success rate on pick-and-place using only a final goal specification, compared to 0% for a single-level world model. Additionally, across physics-based simulated environments including push manipulation and maze navigation, hierarchical planning achieves higher success while requiring up to 3x less planning-time compute.

The paper was published in April 2026 (arXiv 2604.03208).

Based on the search results, here's what I found about the TempoRL paper:

## TempoRL: Learning When to Act

TempoRL addresses temporal abstraction by requiring fewer decisions, and proposes a more proactive setting in which not only an action is chosen in a state but also for how long to commit to that action, showing that this approach is capable of learning successful policies much faster than vanilla Q-learning.

The core motivation behind TempoRL stems from a fundamental issue in traditional reinforcement learning: behaviors are learned in a purely reactive fashion, where an appropriate action is selected based on an observation. In this form, it is challenging to learn when it is necessary to make new decisions. This makes learning inefficient especially in environments with very fine-grained time steps.

Rather than making a decision at every time step, TempoRL proposes a more proactive setting in which not only an action is chosen in a state but also for how long to commit to that action. This allows the agent to learn action repetition or "skip lengths," essentially learning when it needs to reconsider its policy.

The paper includes experiments on various environments, evaluating performance in terms of both reward and the number of decision points made by the agent. This represents a practical approach to temporal abstraction that differs from other frameworks like options, as options require a lot of prior knowledge about the environment to determine the set of admissible states.

## R2-Dreamer: Redundancy-Reduced World Models without Decoders or Augmentation

R2-Dreamer is a decoder-free MBRL framework with a self-supervised objective that serves as an internal regularizer, preventing representation collapse without resorting to data augmentation.

### Key Innovation

The core of the method is a redundancy-reduction objective inspired by Barlow Twins, which can be easily integrated into existing frameworks.

### Performance

On DeepMind Control Suite and Meta-World, R2-Dreamer is competitive with strong baselines such as DreamerV3 and TD-MPC2 while training 1.59x faster than DreamerV3, and yields substantial gains on DMC-Subtle with tiny task-relevant objects.

### Architecture Details

R2-Dreamer features the complete removal of the image decoder and the introduction of a lightweight linear projector head. While DreamerV3 relies on a decoder to reconstruct observations for representation learning, R2-Dreamer's projector simply maps the latent state to the feature space of the image embedding.

## Overview

DyMoDreamer is a novel model-based reinforcement learning (MBRL) algorithm that incorporates a dynamic modulation mechanism to improve the extraction of dynamic features and enrich temporal information.

## Key Technical Components

DyMoDreamer employs differential observations derived from a novel inter-frame differencing mask, explicitly encoding object-level motion cues and temporal dynamics. Dynamic modulation is modeled as stochastic categorical distributions and integrated into a recurrent state-space model (RSSM), enhancing the model's focus on reward-relevant dynamics.

## Architecture Details

The model converts observations into latent stochastic categorical distributions for the latent variable zt, which consists of 32 categories, each with 32 classes. The approach is based on DreamerV3, introducing dynamic modulation into the RSSM world model architecture.

## Performance Results

DyMoDreamer sets a new state-of-the-art on the Atari 100k benchmark with a 156.6% mean human-normalized score, establishes a new record of 832 on the DeepMind Visual Control Suite, and gains a 9.5% performance improvement after 1M steps on the Crafter benchmark.

DyMoDreamer is a novel model-based reinforcement learning (MBRL) algorithm that incorporates a dynamic modulation mechanism to improve the extraction of dynamic features and enrich temporal information.

## Overview

DMWM is a novel dual-mind world model framework that integrates logical reasoning to enable imagination with logical consistency, inspired by the dual-process theory of human cognition.

## Core Components

DMWM is composed of two components: an RSSM-based System 1 (RSSM-S1) component that handles state transitions in an intuitive manner and a logic-integrated neural network-based System 2 (LINN-S2) component that guides the imagination process through hierarchical deep logical reasoning.

## Problem Addressed

Existing recurrent state-space model (RSSM)-based world models depend on single-step statistical inference to capture environment dynamics, and are unable to perform long-term imagination tasks due to accumulation of prediction errors.

## Key Innovation

The inter-system feedback mechanism is designed to ensure that the imagination process follows the logical rules of the real environment.

## Performance Results

Extensive experimental results demonstrate that the proposed framework yields significant improvements in terms of logical coherence, trial efficiency, data efficiency and long-term imagination over state-of-the-art world models. More specifically, DMWM provides 14.3%, 5.5-fold, 32% and 120% improvement in logic consistency, trial efficiency, data efficiency and reliable imagination over extended horizon size compared to baselines in complex tasks.

## Publication

This was published as a NeurIPS 2025 spotlight paper.

## EA-WM: Event-Aware Generative World Model

EA-WM uses Kinematic-to-Visual Action Fields (KVAFs) which bring action conditioning into the same image domain as future video generation, thereby alleviating domain misalignment and providing richer spatial and geometric cues for robotic world modeling.

At the architectural level, EA-WM augments a diffusion-transformer backbone with a dedicated KVAF branch and interval-based bidirectional fusion, facilitating continuous interaction between structured kinematic cues and video features.

**Key Innovation - Event-Difference Latent Supervision (EDLS):**

The model introduces an event-aware bidirectional fusion mechanism driven by Event-Difference Latent Supervision (EDLS). By supervising event predictions with VAE-encoded temporal difference latents, EDLS compels the model to dynamically allocate attention not only to the robot's geometric progression but also to regions undergoing state transitions and interaction dynamics, leading to significantly more physically consistent rollouts.

**Application and Purpose:**

EA-WM is developed for robotic video world modeling and is evaluated in simulation. The model does not directly execute robot actions, nor is it deployed on real robots in this work.

The paper appears to be a recent contribution to the field of video prediction and world modeling for robotics, focusing on improving the physical consistency of predicted video rollouts through attention to temporal differences and interaction dynamics.

Based on the search results, I found highly relevant information about ELVIS:

ELVIS is a latent model predictive controller (MPC) designed to make long-horizon planning practical, which plans in a Dreamer-style recurrent state space model (RSSM) and replaces standard unimodal model predictive path integral (MPPI) with a Gaussian-mixture MPPI that maintains multiple coherent hypotheses over long horizons.

ELVIS stabilizes deep imagination with a shared uncertainty-aware λₜ-return: an ensemble of latent critics defines an upper-confidence-bound (UCB) score that gates a time-varying horizon.

The key innovation is how ELVIS addresses the challenge of long-horizon visual control. When observations are missing, the belief must be propagated by the RSSM prior, increasing epistemic uncertainty and making deep rollouts unreliable unless the controller can decide where the effective horizon should end—this is addressed with a shared uncertainty-aware return used consistently for: (i) learning an imagined actor–critic prior and (ii) scoring MPPI rollouts.

ELVIS combines (i) GMM-MPPI to preserve multi-modal long-horizon hypotheses and avoid mode collapse, and (ii) an ensemble-UCB-gated, time-varying λₜ that softly truncates return propagation and links imagined actor-critic learning with online planning.

Across standard DMControl vision benchmarks, ELVIS improves performance, and ELVIS also achieves strong zero-shot sim-to-real transfer on a real-world sand-spraying task with severe visual occlusions.

The TAWM research experimented with two integration methods: Euler and fourth-order Runge-Kutta (RK4), with RK4 being broadly applicable to both simple linear and complex nonlinear systems and standard in physical simulation. # 2. Related Work

We situate our approach within five related lines of research: fixed-rate model-based RL, variable-rate and temporal abstraction, learned skipping for planning, imagination quality improvement, and event-aware world models.

## 2.1 Model-Based RL with Fixed-Rate Imagination

Modern model-based RL agents learn latent world models and optimize policies through imagined rollouts at a fixed temporal resolution.

DreamerV3 \citep{hafner2023dreamerv3} learns a Recurrent State-Space Model (RSSM) that maintains deterministic and stochastic latent states, training an actor-critic purely through $H$-step imagined trajectories. It achieves strong performance across diverse domains but operates at a fixed one-environment-step-per-latent-step resolution, limiting the effective planning horizon to $H$ environment steps regardless of episode length. NE-Dreamer \citep{nedreamer2026} replaces pixel-level reconstruction with next-embedding prediction, yielding a decoder-free latent world model that improves sample efficiency while retaining the fixed-rate imagination structure. R2-Dreamer \citep{r2dreamer2026} similarly eliminates the observation decoder by training with redundancy-reduced latent targets, accelerating training and improving robustness.
These methods share a fundamental limitation: each imagination step covers exactly one environment timestep, so for long-horizon tasks (e.g., 250-step manipulation episodes), a rollout of $H{=}15$ steps covers only 6\% of the episode, creating a credit assignment bottleneck. Our method addresses this by learning to skip uneventful timesteps, extending the effective horizon to $\sum \Delta t_i$ environment steps (up to $H \times K$) without additional latent computation.

## 2.2 Variable-Rate and Temporal Abstraction

Several works introduce temporal flexibility into world model dynamics, either through externally specified time gaps or learned hierarchical abstractions.

TAWM \citep{freed2024tawm} introduces time-aware world models that condition latent dynamics on a temporal gap $\Delta t$ via RK4/Euler integration, enabling the model to predict across variable time scales. However, $\Delta t$ must be externally specified rather than learned, and TAWM is built on TD-MPC2's short-horizon MPC framework ($H{=}3$--$5$ with MPPI planning), where temporal skipping during planning is counterproductive. Our method adapts the variable-$\Delta t$ conditioning principle to DreamerV3's RSSM but makes $\Delta t$ \emph{state-dependent} via a learned event gate. THICK \citep{romac2024thick} learns a two-level temporal hierarchy via discrete latent dynamics, where the lower level forms invariant contexts and the upper level predicts context changes. While this achieves temporal abstraction, the fixed two-level structure cannot express continuous degrees of event significance or variable skip lengths within a single hierarchy level. HWM \citep{zhang2026hwm} extends this line by learning multi-scale latent world models for hierarchical planning with a learned action encoder for temporal compression, but similarly relies on a fixed two-level planner architecture. ASI \citep{neitz2018adaptive} learns to skip timesteps in recurrent dynamics models by min-pooling over reconstruction losses, selecting intervals that are easiest to predict. It operates on raw observation prediction without integration into a model-based RL loop and optimizes for prediction ease rather than dynamical significance.

Our approach avoids the multi-model exploitation problem identified by \citet{schiewer2024hierarchical} in hierarchical world models by operating within a single RSSM, while offering finer temporal adaptation than two-level hierarchies through a continuous per-step stride selection.

## 2.3 Learned Skipping for Planning

A separate line of work learns explicit skip or jump decisions to extend planning horizons.

LS-Imagine \citep{li2025lsimagine} learns jumping flags based on affordance-map kurtosis for open-world exploration in MineDojo, enabling the agent to skip over low-information states during imagination. The jumps are action-independent and designed for exploration in open-world settings. Our gate differs in two key ways: it operates within the actor-critic MBRL imagination loop with policy-dependent variable-rate stepping, and it selects strides based on latent-state dynamics rather than observation-space affordance maps. I-TAP \citep{itap2026} learns temporal abstractions via discrete residual tokens with an RQ-VAE, performing MCTS planning in token space for offline RL. It operates in a fundamentally different paradigm---offline and autoregressive---from our online RSSM-based approach.

While both LS-Imagine and I-TAP demonstrate the value of temporal flexibility in planning, neither addresses the specific setting of online actor-critic training with variable-rate latent imagination. Our event gate fills this gap by integrating state-dependent stride selection directly into DreamerV3's imagination pipeline.

## 2.4 Imagination Quality Improvement

Rather than changing temporal resolution, several recent works improve the quality of fixed-rate imagination rollouts.

DMWM \citep{wang2025dmwm} introduces a dual-mind architecture combining an RSSM-based System~1 for intuitive transitions with a logic-informed neural network (LINN) System~2 that provides logical reasoning feedback, improving long-horizon imagination coherence through logical constraints. It shares our motivation of extending effective RSSM imagination but addresses error accumulation at fixed temporal resolution rather than extending the temporal horizon. DyMoDreamer \citep{dymodreamer2025} uses inter-frame differencing masks with stochastic categorical dynamic modulation to focus RSSM attention on motion-relevant features, achieving strong results on visual benchmarks (Atari 100k, DMC). It operates at the observation/pixel level to improve per-step representation quality, whereas our method operates in latent space and changes the \emph{temporal resolution} of imagination rather than the attention quality of individual steps---the two approaches target complementary axes of improvement and could in principle be combined. ELVIS \citep{du2026elvis} introduces ensemble-calibrated uncertainty-aware $\lambda$-return gating for long-horizon RSSM-based MPC, adaptively weighting bootstrapping versus continued rollout based on epistemic uncertainty. While ELVIS adapts \emph{how much} to trust each imagination step, it does not change \emph{how many} environment steps each imagination step covers---our gate modifies the temporal resolution itself.

## 2.5 Event-Aware World Models

Event-driven representations have recently been applied to world models, though primarily at the observation level.

EA-WM \citep{eawm2026} introduces event-aware fusion via frame-difference supervision for video world models at the pixel level, using event signals to improve generation quality of dynamic regions. While both EA-WM and our method leverage event-like signals (frame differences vs. latent-state deltas), EA-WM applies them to improve pixel-level video prediction quality, whereas we use latent-state change magnitude to drive \emph{temporal stride selection} in the imagination loop for policy optimization. Our event gate operates entirely in the learned latent space, using state-delta magnitude as a proxy for dynamical significance to determine when fine-grained versus coarse-grained imagination is warranted.
